requirements.text: The immobilizer shall be designed and installed so that the equipped vehicle continues to meet the technical requirements of UN R162.
The immobilizer shall not enter the set state while the ignition key is in the engine running mode.
The immobilizer shall not be capable of being permanently overridden.
The immobilizer shall be designed and built so that, when installed, it does not adversely affect the designed function and safe operation of the vehicle even in the event of a malfunction.

The immobilizer shall be designed and built so that it cannot be rapidly and without attracting attention rendered ineffective or destroyed using low-cost, easily concealed tools, equipment or fabrications.
The immobilizer shall be designed so that replacing a major component or assembly to bypass it is difficult and time-consuming.
The immobilizer shall be able to withstand the in-vehicle environment for a reasonable lifetime when installed as specified by the manufacturer.
The immobilizer shall not adversely affect the electrical properties of the on-board circuitry (lead cross-sections, contact safety, etc.).
The immobilizer shall not prevent the release of the vehicle's brakes.
The immobilizer shall not operate in a manner that applies the brakes of the vehicle.
The immobilizer shall prevent operation of the vehicle under its own motive power by interference by code with at least one control unit required for vehicle operation.
The immobilizer, when fitted to a vehicle equipped with a catalytic converter, shall not cause unburnt fuel to enter the exhaust.
The immobilizer shall not change its set/unset state as a result of any of the tests in paragraph 5.3.

The immobilizer shall set without supplementary action from the driver, at least by turning the ignition key to the "0" position and activating a door or at the latest 1 minute after removing the key.
The electronic unsetting device of the immobilizer shall provide at least 50,000 variants and shall incorporate rolling codes and/or have a minimum scan time of ten days.
Where the immobilizer indicates short-term set/unset changes optically using the direction indicators, that indication shall not exceed 3 seconds.
All components of the immobilizer shall be subjected to the tests described in Annex 6.
All components of the immobilizer shall operate without any failure under the climatic, protection, weatherability and electrical conditions of Annex 6.
Immobilizer parts fitted in the passenger or luggage compartment shall operate from -40 °C to +85 °C.
Immobilizer parts fitted in the engine compartment shall operate from -40 °C to +125 °C unless otherwise specified.
Immobilizer parts fitted in the passenger compartment shall provide degree of protection IP 40 in accordance with IEC Publication 529:1989.
Immobilizer parts fitted elsewhere than in the passenger compartment shall provide degree of protection IP 54.
The immobilizer shall withstand a weatherability test of 7 days according to IEC 68-2-30-1980.
The immobilizer shall operate with a supply voltage from 9 V to 15 V over the temperature range of Annex 6 paragraph 1.1.
After completion of all Annex 6 tests, the immobilizer shall continue to function normally when tested at 12 ± 0.2 V and 23 ± 5 °C.
The immobilizer shall continue to operate normally after 4 hours storage at -40 ± 2 °C with a test voltage of 9 ± 0.2 V.
Passenger or luggage compartment parts shall continue to operate normally after 4 hours storage at +85 ± 2 °C with a test voltage of 15 ± 0.2 V.
The immobilizer shall withstand an excess voltage of 18 ± 0.2 V for 1 hour in both set and unset states.
The immobilizer shall withstand an excess voltage of 24 ± 0.2 V for 1 minute in both set and unset states.
The immobilizer shall continue to operate normally after the foreign body and water-tightness test according to IEC 529-1989.
The immobilizer shall continue to operate normally after the resistance-to-humidity test according to IEC 68-2-30 (1980).
The immobilizer and its components shall not be destroyed by reversed polarity up to 13 V during 2 minutes.
All electrical connections of the immobilizer shall be short-circuit proof against earth up to max. 13 V and/or fused.
The energy consumption of the complete immobilizer including status display in set condition shall not exceed 20 mA on average.
Vehicle-mounted (Type 1) immobilizer components shall withstand sinusoidal vibration from 10 Hz to 500 Hz at max. amplitude ± 5 mm and max. acceleration 3 g (0-peak).
Engine-attached (Type 2) immobilizer components shall withstand sinusoidal vibration from 20 Hz to 300 Hz at max. amplitude ± 2 mm and max. acceleration 15 g (0-peak).
The vibration test shall be performed at 1 octave/min with 10 cycles along each of the 3 axes.
The immobilizer shall continue to operate normally after the vibration test.
The immobilizer shall be subjected to the electromagnetic compatibility tests described in Annex 7.
The immobilizer shall be tested for immunity to conducted disturbances along supply lines in both unset and set states.
When tested for radiated high frequency immunity in the set state with Key OFF, the immobilizer shall show no unexpected deactivation of the immobilizer.
When tested for radiated high frequency immunity in the unset state (Key ON or vehicle at 50 km/h), the immobilizer shall show no unexpected activation.
The immobilizer shall be tested for immunity to electrostatic discharges in accordance with ISO 10605-2008 + corrigendum:2010 + AMD1:2014 at the levels of Table 2.

The immobilizer in set state, at externally accessible points with the vehicle locked and Key OFF, shall withstand ± 15 kV air discharge without unexpected deactivation without reactivation within 1 s.

The immobilizer in set state, at externally accessible points with the vehicle locked and Key OFF, shall withstand ± 8 kV contact discharge without unexpected deactivation without reactivation within 1 s.
Each ESD test shall be performed with 3 discharges with a minimum of 5 s interval between each discharge.
Radiated emissions of the immobilizer shall be tested according to UN Regulation No. 10, 06 series, with the immobilizer in set state.
For the 12 V system, the ESA shall not emit transient conducted disturbances on supply lines exceeding +75 V (positive) and -100 V (negative).
The ESA, for transient pulse 1 on the 12 V system, shall meet functional performance status classification III for immunity related functions at -75 V over 500 pulses.
The ESA shall meet functional performance status classification I for pulse 2a (+37 V, 500 pulses) and II for pulse 2b (+10 V, 10 pulses) on the 12 V system.
The ESA shall meet functional performance status classification I for pulses 3a (-112 V) and 3b (+75 V), each applied for 1 h on the 12 V system.

The ESA shall withstand radiated electromagnetic immunity test levels of 60 V/m (stripline), 75 V/m (TEM cell), 60 mA (BCI), 30 V/m (ALSE) and 21 V/m (reverberation) below 2 GHz over 90 per cent of the band.
The ESA shall withstand radiated electromagnetic immunity test levels of 10 V/m (ALSE) and 7 V/m (reverberation chamber) between 2,000 and 6,000 MHz.
During radiated immunity testing, the ESA shall show no degradation of performance of immunity related functions.
The narrowband radiated emissions of the ESA shall be below 52 to 42 dBµV/m from 30 to 75 MHz, 42 to 53 dBµV/m from 75 to 400 MHz and 53 dBµV/m from 400 to 1,000 MHz.
The broadband radiated emissions of the ESA shall be below 62 to 52 dBµV/m from 30 to 75 MHz, 52 to 63 dBµV/m from 75 to 400 MHz and 63 dBµV/m from 400 to 1,000 MHz.
